chunks: From him, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man hears testimony and is not called upon to testify against it, he has the choice: if he wishes, he testifies; if he wishes, he remains silent. However, if he knows the oppressed party, he must testify, and it is not permissible for him to remain silent."

key_terms.يُشْهَدْ: To be called upon to testify

ai.seo_question: When is a witness obligated to testify if they are not directly summoned?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between general discretion (*ikhtiyar*) and obligatory testimony (*wujub*) based on the witness's knowledge of the specific oppressed party. This ruling underscores the duty of *Shahadat al-Khas* (specific testimony) to prevent injustice, a concept deeply rooted in the Imams' teachings on social accountability. It highlights the transition from passive silence to active legal participation when the identity of the claimant is known.
